findings.message: SPEC-4's entire body is wrapped in `if [[ -f "$_rl_guard" ]]; then ... fi` with no `else` clause, so if `review-lens/plugin.sh` is absent the assertion silently produces no output (neither pass nor fail), while every other new SPEC (2, 3, 5, 6) fires `assert_fail` for a missing file because `grep -q ... 2>/dev/null` returns non-zero.

The file-level header comment still reads "`review-lens` still calls bare `extract_first_json_object`" (lines 10-11), which directly contradicts SPEC-4's new assertion that no non-comment code line uses `extract_first_json_object`; the issue required this comment to be updated but the change left it stale.

The SPEC-3 block comment still says "review-lens is the counter-example… It is allowed to stay on `extract_first_json_object`" (lines 88-89), but post-migration SPEC-3 always takes the migrated branch (line 106); the comment now describes a branch the test can never reach under normal conditions, creating misleading documentation about the test's actual control flow.
